item.title: Subterranean tunnel, possibly used for medieval cult rituals, discovered in Stone Age tomb in Germany
item.description: A tunnel system discovered in a Stone Age tomb in Germany suggests medieval people created hiding places for their cultic rituals.

item.title: NASA telescope spots the building blocks for life spewing out of comet 3I/ATLAS
item.description: NASA's SPHEREx space telescope detected organic molecules coming off comet 3I/ATLAS as the interstellar visitor made its closest approach to Earth in December.

item.title: Archaeopteryx, one of the world's first proto birds, has a set of weird, never-before-seen features, new study reveals
item.description: Iconic transition species between dinosaurs and birds may have had weird 'teeth' on roof of its mouth and a highly mobile tongue, study reveals

item.title: Canada could remove 5 times its annual carbon emissions by planting trees on edge of boreal forest, study finds
item.description: Planting trees on 6.4 million hectares of northern taiga forest could remove 3.9 gigatons of CO2 by 2100 — five times Canada's annual emissions.

item.title: Record-breaking gravitational wave puts Einstein's relativity to its toughest test yet — and proves him right again
item.description: A record-breaking gravitational wave signal let scientists "listen" to a distant black hole merger and put Einstein's gravity to its toughest test yet.

item.title: 'It's telling us there's something big going on': Unprecedented spike in atmospheric methane during the COVID-19 pandemic has a troubling explanation
item.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the atmosphere temporarily lost its ability to break down methane, leading to a huge spike in the greenhouse gas.

item.title: Did modern humans wipe out the Neanderthals? New evidence may finally provide answers.
item.description: A complex picture of how Neanderthals died out, and the role that modern humans played in their disappearance, is emerging.

item.title: Newly visible, city-size 'green comet' will soon be ejected into interstellar space — just like 3I/ATLAS
item.description: Comet Wierzchoś, also known as C/2024 E1, is rapidly brightening as it approaches its closest point to Earth next week. But experts predict it will eventually be thrown out of the solar system forever, just like the "alien" comet 3I/ATLAS.

item.title: MIT designs computing component that uses waste heat 'as a form of information'
item.description: Proof of concept uses passive components to redirect heat across a chip, allowing temperature patterns to be used for data processing.

item.title: Trump is bringing car pollution and other greenhouse gases back to America's skies. Here are the health risks we all face from climate change.
item.description: Four researchers dive into the health risks associated with climate change, and why the recent decision by the Trump administration to rescind key environmental policies could lead to serious harm.
